missions.planned_outcome: Produce an ONBOARDING.md for this Nelson fork covering repo layout, plugin surfaces, and current in-flight state, plus a ranked improvement backlog in the captain's log
missions.actual_outcome: DASHBOARD.md produced at repo root: a phase-organized state-model explainer plus a two-mission worked-example walkthrough (this mission as the healthy case, the stale 2026-07-06 mission as the cautionary case), admiral-validated against the real on-disk files.
missions.success_metric: ONBOARDING.md lands at repo root, reviewed; captain's log carries a ranked improvement backlog with effort/impact notes; stale mission state is reported, not fixed
missions.success_metric_result: DASHBOARD.md exists, reviewed by the admiral field-by-field against this mission's and the stale mission's real files (all matched); ranked improvement backlog with dashboard-tool proposal to follow in captains-log.md; stale mission reported, not touched.

adopt: Using the live, currently-running mission as its own worked example for documentation — every claim is independently re-checkable against real files, not invented illustrative JSON.
Resolving a becalmed-fleet vs admiral-at-the-helm tension by using subagents mode with exactly one captain, rather than defaulting to single-session when the task involves real implementation work.
avoid: Amending sailing-orders.json by direct edit without a matching nelson-data.py subcommand leaves fleet-status.json's cached mission.outcome field stale.

nelson-data.py event --type task_completed accepts no per-type data fields in this installed version, despite references/structured-data.md documenting --task-id/--owner/etc.; nelson-phase.py's UNDERWAY exit check requires data.task_id, so the documented CLI usage cannot actually unblock phase advance without a direct JSON edit.
